ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Shown in the diagram is a graph of $f'$, the derivative of function $f$. If $f(3)=3$, then what is $f(1)$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: What is given in the figure is the graph of f', an upward-sloping straight line. This straight line passes through the point (0,-2) on the y-axis, and passes through the point (3,0) on the x-axis. Reasoning: From the two points (0,-2) and (3,0), the slope can be obtained as (0-(-2))/(3-0)=2/3, so f'(x)=(2/3)x-2. According to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, f(3)-f(1)=∫_1^3 f'(x) dx=∫_1^3 ((2/3)x-2) dx. Calculating gives ∫_1^3 ((2/3)x-2) dx = [x^2/3-2x]_1^3 = -4/3. Therefore 3-f(1)=-4/3, and solving gives f(1)=13/3.
